newsitem.title: USA: U.S spot resids steady to up despite crude selloff.
newsitem.headline: U.S spot resids steady to up despite crude selloff.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly held steady Friday in lackluster activity despite a sharp selloff in crude, helped by reports of better utility interest after some cool weather on the East Coast.
"There have been a few utilities stepping up to buy oil this week, but next week, the weather doesn't look that supportive and there's still plenty of oil," said one trader.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent was still quoted on either side of $18 a barrel, with Feb paper gaining almost 50 cents to the $18 level despite weaker crude. Traders said March paper firmed slightly to the $17.75-18.00 level.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour gained 25 cents to $19.50 after reports NYPA Thursday awarded a third 100,000-barrel piece for 2/3-7 delivery at $20 (delivered), traders said.
High sulphur in New York again was unchanged, but some said refinery unit outages in the Gulf could mean enough HSFO on the market to pressure prices there.
Traders said coker maintenance until mid-February at a Star refinery in Texas meant an additional 50,000 bpd of HSFO on the market.
U.S. Gulf prices also held steady, with no deals reported.
New York city gate weekend gas prices skidded another 15 cents to the mid-$3.40s/mmBtu. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.85/mmBtu equivalent.
